To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a research-based approach is the most effective way to integrate graduate attributes into the curriculum, assessment and teaching of a unit of study.

1) the integration of a graduate attributes policy into assessment tasks and assessment rubrics is a worthwhile endeavour; 2) this integration can be facilitated through the use of a software application designed for this purpose; 3) the integration of the graduate attributes policy into the assessment tasks and rubrics can be achieved through a research-based approach; and 4) the integration of graduate attributes into the assessment tasks is a worthwhile endeavour.

the process of integrating graduate attributes into a business law unit can be facilitated by the use of software that allows academics to: • identify and code assessment tasks to attribute categories; • identify and code criteria to attribute categories; and • map the assessment tasks to the assessment criteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how can assessment be used to assess the development of graduate attributes in the business law curriculum?
the development of an assessment strategy that is both transparent and effective, and which can be applied to any discipline or unit of study.
the question: ‘What can law teachers learn about the integration of graduate attributes into the assessment of business law subjects?’
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
graduate attribute assessment is a complex and challenging task.
graduate attributes can be successfully integrated into the curriculum and assessment processes of a business law unit, and that the benefits to students are significant.
it is possible to integrate graduate attributes with assessment and to provide feedback on the development of attributes to students.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integration of graduate attributes in the curriculum is a worthwhile endeavour but that the process is not straightforward.
the integration of graduate attributes in the assessment process is a worthwhile endeavour, and that it can be done, but it takes effort and persistence.
it is possible to embed graduate attributes in the curriculum and in assessment processes in such a way that students are aware of and can demonstrate their progress in developing the attributes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the implementation of a graduate attributes policy is not simply about the inclusion of a new category in a unit’s assessment criteria.

graduate attribute mapping is not a one-off task, but a process that requires regular review to ensure that assessment tasks and assessment processes remain aligned with graduate attribute categories.
graduate attributes can be embedded in the curriculum in a way that enhances learning and assessment, and provides feedback to students.
